---
title: One million orders, one Parquet file
description: Twelve charts and a table that each read an aggregate of one large Parquet file, and a chart that reads a small one whole.
version: 0.0.1
slug: parquet-report
---

## Every chart asks the file for its own few rows

The report folder holds `data/orders.parquet`: one million synthetic orders of a fictional retailer in eleven columns, about 3.54 MB on disk. No chart below embeds those rows. Each names a SQL query in `queries/`, the query aggregates the file, and the chart embeds the result: 24 months, 8 categories, 40 cells.

```callout
kind: neutral
title: Where the data comes from
body: "`report.connectors.yaml` declares the file as the `orders` connector of kind `parquet`, and each query reads it as the table `orders`. RichView runs the query in a confined process that can read that one file and nothing else. The rendered HTML holds each chart's aggregated rows, labelled as a query's result, and never the file."
```

## Growth and season

```chart
type: line
title: Revenue grew from 5.45 million in January 2024 to 23.5 million in October 2025
subtitle: Revenue per month, synthetic orders
data:
  sql:
    connector: orders
    query: queries/revenue-by-month.sql
encoding: {x: month, y: revenue}
axes:
  x: {label: Month}
  y: {label: Revenue, format: number_compact}
```

*Source: `data/orders.parquet`, synthetic orders, aggregated by `queries/revenue-by-month.sql`.*

```chart
type: line
title: West leads and North trails in every month
subtitle: Revenue per month by region, synthetic orders
data:
  sql:
    connector: orders
    query: queries/revenue-by-month-and-region.sql
encoding: {x: month, y: revenue, color: region}
axes:
  x: {label: Month}
  y: {label: Revenue, format: number_compact}
```

*Source: `data/orders.parquet`, synthetic orders, aggregated by `queries/revenue-by-month-and-region.sql`.*

```table
title: The twelve stores with the most revenue
data:
  sql:
    connector: orders
    query: queries/store-table.sql
columns:
  - {key: store, label: Store}
  - {key: city, label: City}
  - {key: region, label: Region}
  - {key: orders, label: Orders, format: number, align: right}
  - {key: revenue, label: Revenue, format: number, align: right}
  - {key: order_value, label: Average order, format: number, align: right}
  - {key: returned_per_thousand, label: "Returned in 1,000", format: number, align: right}
```

*Source: `data/orders.parquet`, synthetic orders, aggregated by `queries/store-table.sql`.*

## A small file, read whole

`data/stores.parquet` holds the forty stores. The chart below names the file itself in `data.parquet`: RichView reads the one column the chart uses, every row of it, and the chart counts the stores in each size band.

```chart
type: histogram
title: "Most stores are small: 22 of the 40 are under 1,000 square metres"
subtitle: Floor area of the forty stores, synthetic
data: {parquet: data/stores.parquet}
encoding: {x: floor_area_m2}
binning: {count: 8}
axes:
  x: {label: Floor area (square metres)}
  y: {label: Stores}
```

*Source: `data/stores.parquet`, synthetic stores.*
